test_title: PYST 14: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the function of the "Speak Up!" portal launched by NADA (National Anti Doping Agency)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Report Anti-Doping Rule Violations confidentially**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** India launched the **"Speak Up!"** portal as a secure and confidential digital platform dedicated to reporting **Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRV)**. This function allows individuals to report suspicious activities without fear of repercussions. ***Hence, the statement regarding reporting violations is correct.***
 
• The primary **use** of this portal is to protect the **integrity** of sports in **India** by encouraging **whistleblowers**, including **athletes**, **coaches**, and **support personnel**, to share sensitive information about doping.
 
• The **"Speak Up!"** portal ensures **anonymity**, meaning the identity of the informant is strictly protected under the guidelines of the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**. This **feature** is critical for gathering intelligence that may not be available through routine testing.
 
• The portal is a key component of **NADA's** **Intelligence and Investigations** framework. It focuses on catching not just the athletes who use **banned substances**, but also the wider network of **suppliers** and **facilitators** involved in doping rings.
 
• By providing a dedicated **online platform**, **NADA** aims to foster a **clean sports culture** where stakeholders feel empowered to contribute to a **dope-free environment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA):** It was established as a registered society under the **Societies Registration Act** on **November 24, 2005**. It functions under the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of **India**.
 
• **WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency):** Founded on **November 10, 1999**, in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, and now headquartered in **Montreal, Canada**. **WADA** sets the **Global Anti-Doping Code**, which **NADA** India follows to maintain international standards in **drug testing** and **adjudication**.
 
• **Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUE):** This is a process where an **athlete** can request permission to use a **prohibited substance** for legitimate **medical reasons**. Applications are reviewed by a **TUE Committee** consisting of **medical experts** to ensure no unfair advantage is gained.
 
• **Banned Substances:** These are listed annually by **WADA** in the **Prohibited List**. Categories include **Anabolic Agents**, **Peptide Hormones**, **Stimulants**, and **Glucocorticoids**. The list is updated every **year**, effective from **January 1st**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRV):** Under the **2021 WADA Code**, there are **11** distinct violations. These include the **presence** of a substance, **attempted use**, **refusing** a sample collection, **whereabouts failures**, and **trafficking**.
 
• **Dope Testing Process:** **NADA** conducts both **In-Competition** and **Out-of-Competition** testing. Samples (blood or urine) are analyzed at **WADA-accredited laboratories**. In **India**, the **National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL)** is the primary facility for analysis.
 
• **Consequences of Doping:** Athletes found guilty of an **ADRV** face sanctions including **disqualification** of results, **forfeiture** of medals, and **period of ineligibility** (bans) ranging from a **few months** to a **lifetime ban** for repeat offenders.
 
• **The Registered Testing Pool (RTP):** High-level athletes must provide their **location** and **contact details** for **one hour** every **day** to allow for **unannounced testing**. Failure to provide this **data** three times in **12 months** constitutes an **ADRV**.
